# Domain reference: Tech

Job family covered: Software Engineer, Product Manager, Data (Scientist / Analyst / Engineer), DevOps / SRE / Platform, QA / SDET.

---

## Software Engineer

### Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Staff+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Design & code | Writes working, readable, tested code. Understands basic data structures. | Production-quality code. Masters common patterns, unit and integration tests. | Designs complex modules. Arbitrates between solutions, documents technical choices. | Defines code and architecture standards for an organization. |
| Problem solving | Debugs methodically. Identifies edge cases with help. | Diagnoses complex problems. Proposes several approaches and compares the trade-offs. | Solves cross-cutting problems involving several systems. Anticipates side effects. | Identifies systemic problems and proposes structural solutions at organization scale. |
| System architecture | Understands the interactions between components. | Designs services or components autonomously. | Designs distributed systems, evaluates scalability and resilience. | Defines the architectural vision, arbitrates strategic technology choices. |

### Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Staff+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technical leadership | Takes part in code reviews. | Leads reviews, proposes process improvements. | Mentors, influences the team's technical decisions. | Sets the standard others follow, defines the technical culture, contributes to hiring. |
| Cross-functional collaboration | Communicates clearly within the team. | Works with PM/Design on specs. | Aligns several teams on technical choices. | Influences the tech direction with C-level stakeholders. |

### Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Technology watch | Follows developments, evaluates new technologies for the team's context. |
| Process contribution | Improves the tools, CI/CD, and the team's practices. |
| Written communication | Documents choices, writes ADRs (architecture decision records) and post-mortems. |

---

## Product Manager

### Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Product Leadership |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Product strategy | Executes the defined roadmap. Writes user stories. | Builds and defends a roadmap. Prioritizes with frameworks (RICE, ICE). | Defines the product vision, positions against the competition. | Manages a product portfolio, aligns the product strategy with the business strategy. |
| User focus | Conducts interviews, synthesizes feedback. | Designs research plans, interprets qualitative/quantitative data. | Defines the research strategy, anticipates unexpressed needs. | Creates a user-centered culture in the organization. |
| Data-driven management | Tracks product metrics, produces dashboards. | Designs experiments (A/B tests), interprets results with statistical rigor. | Defines the business metrics, links product indicators to the P&L. | Manages the performance of a portfolio with financial KPIs. |

### Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Product Leadership |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cross-functional leadership | Coordinates the product/tech/design team. | Aligns stakeholders, handles priority conflicts. | Influences without hierarchical authority, carries difficult trade-offs. | Leads product transformations, manages PMs. |
| Business acumen | Understands the business model. | Builds business cases, evaluates ROI. | Manages a product P&L, negotiates budgets. | Contributes to corporate strategy, engages with the board. |

### Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Technical literacy | Understands the architecture, discusses technical constraints with developers. |
| Go-to-market | Coordinates launches, collaborates with marketing and sales. |

---

## Data (Scientist / Analyst / Engineer)

### Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statistical analysis | Descriptive statistics, hypothesis tests, visualization. | Advanced modeling, experimental design, causal inference. | Analytical strategy, innovative methodologies, statistical mentoring. |
| Technical mastery | Python/R, SQL, visualization tools. | Advanced ML, feature engineering, data pipelines. | Data architecture, ML systems in production, technology choices. |
| Business impact | Interprets results, produces recommendations. | Translates insights into measurable business actions. | Defines the data strategy, aligns data initiatives with business objectives. |

### Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Description by level |
|---|---|
| Communicating results | Junior: presents clearly. Experienced: adapts to the audience (tech/business). Senior: influences strategic decisions with data. |
| Data engineering | Junior: basic ETL. Experienced: robust pipelines. Senior: data platform architecture. |

---

## DevOps / SRE / Platform

### Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure & automation | Scripts, basic monitoring, cloud 101. | IaC (Terraform/Pulumi), advanced CI/CD, containerization. | Platform architecture, multi-cloud, automation strategy. |
| Reliability & observability | Monitoring, alerting, troubleshooting. | SLI/SLO, incident management, capacity planning. | Reliability strategy, resilience engineering, post-incident review. |
| Security | Basic good practices, access management. | Security automation, compliance, hardening. | Security strategy, governance, audit. |

### Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Developer experience | Improves the tools and workflows of the dev teams. Self-service, documentation, feedback loops. |
| Incident management | Coordination in crisis situations, communication, post-mortem, continuous improvement. |

---

## Cross-cutting tech signals

These signals apply regardless of the tech role:

### Red flags (Red)
- Unable to explain their own past technical choices
- No mention of testing or quality in their practice
- Systematically blames other teams without introspection

### Red flags (Orange)
- Difficulty explaining things to a non-technical audience
- No curiosity about the business context of the product
- Exclusively theoretical answers with no concrete examples of things they delivered
